SR300: 4 scoops of 43 cc = 120 g; timer max 9.9 min. Sources describe fixed heat settings (390/455/490 F targets) and no temperature readout, so no readout is assumed; an owner-added probe is not supported by this entry. Discontinued/legacy model. Row count 12 is the owner's rule for the whole Fresh Roast SR series (10 min is about the longest anyone roasts on it, +2 buffer).

The one CALIBRATED roaster (owner's logged roasts, in F). Retailer: washed 8 oz / 227 g, natural 6 oz / 170 g, minimum roast 4 oz / 113 g; real-time temperature readout, sensor type unstated. Retailer text says total roast 8-18 min and timer to 20 min, but the owner's experience is 10 min at most, so 12 rows per the owner's rule. Chart anchors (145 F start, 270 F at 30 s) are the app's original live-chart constants, tuned on the SR800.

250 g (200 g for natural process, per Sweet Maria's). Manufacturer's roast chart runs 12 min (Light) to 23 min (Italian); timer 1-23 min; setpoint 374-482 F. Display alternates target and actual temperature; heating is indirect air under a thermostat, so chamber air is assumed (sources do not say what 'actual' measures).
300 g; temperature range 140-500 F; Bluetooth/app, variable drum and fan speed. Roast-time chart is the CBR-101's (12-23 min), assumed to apply.

One thermocouple; manual says the display shows roasting-chamber temperature, which reads well above actual bean temperature. Time 10:00-25:00, target temperature 167-428 F, display switchable F/C. External cooling tray.

Two K-type thermocouples (bean and environment); the roast target is bean temperature. Retailer: roasts up to 300 g (250 g on other current models). Time 10:00-25:00, target temperature 167-428 F, display switchable F/C.
Programmable model: 8 segments of up to 3 min, maximum program 22:00 (plus automatic warm-up). Display shows roasting-chamber temperature. Discontinued in the US.

LOW CONFIDENCE: only one review was read. It reports a 500 g maximum, 330 g as the ideal batch, and two thermometers (analog on the drum plus a digital probe). The 150 g minimum and 8-15 min roast time come from a search-result summary only. Unit and probe role assumed.

100 g green (about 90 g roasted); refurbished units 50 g. Recipes typically 6-10 min, hard maximum 12 min. Measures INLET air temperature after the heater (not bean temperature); inlet temperature can reach 290 C (554 F), so the temperature cap is raised to 300 C.

Brochure: 60 g capacity, roast time 0-20 min, samples typically 5-10 min, two sensors (inlet and exhaust). Short roasts are normal, so the roast-time and first-crack floors are lowered. Row count sized to typical roasts, not the 20-min machine limit. Measures INLET air temperature after the heater (not bean temperature); inlet temperature can reach 290 C (554 F), so the temperature cap is raised to 300 C.

Nano 7: 120 g standard batch; 50-200 g with the optional Boost kit (the maximum allows for it). Roast Companion: probe touches the beans (reads 5-10 C above true bean-surface temperature); first crack about 205 C; roast usually ended 220-230 C; profile = temperature curve plus fan curve, ended by a 'roast level'. Typical roast under 10 min; cool-down 2-3 min.

Retailer: capacity 200 g, max 250 g. Gas burner required. Ships with a Celsius analog thermometer in the drum (digital probe optional); reviewers report 8-15 min roasts with first crack around 7-8 min. Where the thermometer sits relative to the beans is not stated, so chamber air is assumed.

Retailers list 200 g. Two probes (bean and environment). Manufacturer M2 page lists roasting time 4-15 min; row count assumed the same across the M-series. Unit assumed C.

Two US retailers list 500 g; a third lists 400 g, so the larger is used to avoid rejecting valid roasts. One search result gave a 50 g minimum (not read on the page). Two probes (bean and environment). Manufacturer M2 page lists roasting time 4-15 min; row count assumed the same across the M-series. Unit assumed C.

Retailer guide: capacity 5 oz (142 g), 4 oz (113 g) recommended for evenness. Roast time is set in minutes and cooling starts automatically 5 min before the end; a retailer blurb (search result) says 20-30 min. Timer only; no temperature readout described.

Article lists a Nostalgia with a solid 4.5 in chamber and a very strong fan (needs a chimney extender to keep beans in). Hot-air popcorn popper (no thermometer). Sources rate chamber depth: a 4.5 in chamber roasts about 90 g; 3.5 in chambers less. Typical 5-10 min (search-result snippet). Batch limits derived from the chamber-depth guideline.
Handheld ceramic roaster: 30-70 g per batch, 50-60 g recommended (another retailer says 30 g). Roast time 3-10 min from a search snippet. No thermometer.
LOW CONFIDENCE: the article covers other Presto models (a 3.5 in chamber), not the PopLite. Batch limits assumed for a small-chamber popper; Presto poppers tend to roast fast and can blow beans out.

M3: handbook batch 250-300 g (cooling bin handles about 300 g or less). Handbook: temperatures are in Celsius; ships with one analog thermometer, ports for bean (BT) and environment (ET) probes; BT reading varies with probe placement and batch size; overall roast 11-22 min; first crack about 205 C. Royal Coffee reports 225 g as a full M3s load.

Previous-generation flagship; its page repeats the L200 spec text. Dual/single bean-temperature probe; 50-200 g per batch; 4-7 min per 200 g batch. Row count and unit assumed.

7 min per 200 g batch. Dual/single bean-temperature probe; 50-200 g per batch; 4-7 min per 200 g batch. Row count and unit assumed.

FAQ: recommended 200-550 g +/- 20 g; first crack at 175-185 C; preheat 8-10 min at 180-220 C; auto-stops after 20 min. Row count assumed larger than the R1 for bigger batches.

Stovetop popper with a hand crank. Source: 8 oz batch, about 10 min total, first crack at 5-7 min. No thermometer unless the owner adds one (source used a probe and an IR thermometer); not supported by this entry.
